transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. 

Um... I feel a little silly even bringing this up, because it's really not a huge deal or anything. But... well, what finally made me ask for help is that I just keep forgetting little things that I normally handle just fine. Like, um, returning phone calls—which is a bit embarrassing since I'm a secretary and I'm usually good at that—or remembering to turn in a registration form, or just stopping for a quick errand on my way home. 

It's really just small stuff like that, you know? Nothing terrible! I'm definitely not falling apart or anything. I just thought maybe I should ask someone about it, just to be safe. I hope it's okay that I made an appointment for something so minor... does that make sense?
When did you first start noticing these memory slips, and have they been happening gradually over months or did they come on more suddenly?

Um, well, I guess... I think it really started to be something I noticed maybe a little over a year ago? About 15 months ago, actually. 

I decided to start this evening certificate program—which is great, really! I'm super lucky to be able to take classes. But I think, um, since I started that, keeping track of my schedule and staying organized has just gotten a tiny bit harder to manage. It definitely wasn't sudden, like I just woke up one day and couldn't remember anything. It just sort of... gradually crept up on me once I had those evening classes to juggle on top of work. 

It's probably totally normal to get a little scattered when you add things to your plate, right? I just hope I'm not making a mountain out of a molehill... does that answer your question?
Have you noticed yourself feeling unusually worried, tense, or on edge over the past year, even about things unrelated to your memory?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I definitely don't feel unusually tense or on edge or anything like that. 

I guess I worry a little bit sometimes, but just normal things, you know? Like making sure I get my assignments done on time or hoping I didn't forget to pass along a message at work. Just the usual stuff anyone would worry about when they're busy. I'm definitely not an anxious person overall. I usually try to just go with the flow and stay positive! 

I hope that's okay to say... I just don't want you to think I'm, like, a nervous wreck or anything, because I'm really not. Does that make sense?
Over the past year, have you noticed any changes in your mood, such as feeling down, losing interest in things you used to enjoy, or having less energy than usual?

Oh, um, no, not at all. My mood has been really good, actually! I definitely haven't felt down or sad or anything like that. And I still really enjoy all my normal hobbies... well, when I actually have the time for them between work and school, anyway! 

I mean, I get a little tired sometimes, but just the normal amount of tired from having a busy schedule, you know? Nothing extreme where I have no energy at all. I'm a pretty upbeat person overall, so I haven't noticed any big changes there. 

Is it okay that I don't have any of those symptoms? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information... I hope I'm being helpful!
Have you had any recent illnesses, head injuries, infections, or been diagnosed with any medical conditions in the past year or so that your doctor mentioned could affect your brain or memory?

Oh, um, no. No, nothing like that at all. I've been really healthy, thankfully! No head injuries or... or bad infections or anything. 

I just go for my regular check-ups, and my doctor always says everything looks great. I try to take really good care of myself, you know, especially with work and school... I really don't want to let my boss or my teachers down by getting sick or missing days. So, yeah, no medical stuff. 

I hope that's okay? I mean, I know a medical reason would probably make this all easier for you to figure out, and I'm sorry if this makes it trickier, but I promise I'm not leaving anything out! Am I doing okay with these questions?
Have any coworkers, friends, or family members noticed or commented on you forgetting things or making mistakes, or is this something only you have noticed?

Um, well... I guess people have noticed a little bit, maybe? Nothing major, I promise! I'm still getting by just fine. 

It's just... well, at work, I've missed a couple of small follow-ups. Just little things, really. And maybe a few minor deadlines for my classes. My boss did mention something the other day, just checking in to make sure I was okay because I forgot to send an email he asked for. It wasn't a huge deal, but... I do worry about it a little. I really want to move up to an Office Manager role eventually, and I just... I want them to think I'm reliable, you know? I don't want these little slip-ups to ruin my reputation or make them think I don't care, because I really do care! 

I try so hard to keep everything organized. Does that make sense? I hope it doesn't make me sound like a terrible employee... I really do try my best!
How many hours of sleep have you been getting each night since you started your evening classes, and do you feel rested during the day?

Um, well, I usually get around... maybe six or seven hours? I think that's pretty normal, right? I mean, I try to get to bed at a decent time after my classes, but sometimes I just need a little bit to wind down, you know? 

I feel mostly fine during the day! Just, you know, the regular amount of tired you'd expect from working and going to school. I definitely don't fall asleep at my desk or anything embarrassing like that. I always have a cup of coffee in the morning and I'm good to go. 

I really try to make sure I'm well-rested so I can be on top of things for my boss. I hope six or seven hours is okay? I know they say eight is best, but I'm doing my best to balance it all... I'm not doing it wrong, am I?

Aside from forgetting tasks or deadlines, have you noticed any difficulty finding the right words in conversation, getting confused about directions or familiar places, or trouble learning new information?

Oh, um, no, nothing like that at all! I'm actually really good with talking to people and finding the right words. I mean, answering phones and greeting people is a huge part of my job, so I always make sure I'm communicating clearly. I definitely don't want anyone at the office thinking I sound unprofessional! 

And no, I never get lost or confused about where I am or anything like that. I know my way around just fine. As for learning new things, I feel like I pick up on new office software or my class material pretty quickly, actually. It's really just... you know, keeping track of the little deadlines sometimes like I mentioned. But my brain feels totally sharp otherwise, I promise! 

I hope that helps narrow things down for you? I always worry I'm not explaining things right, but I'm doing okay with my answers, right?
Can you tell me about your typical caffeine intake, and whether you use alcohol, recreational drugs, or any over-the-counter or prescription medications on a regular basis?

Oh, um, just the coffee I mentioned earlier! Usually just one cup in the morning to get me started. If the office is super busy or I have a ton of reading for class, I might grab a second cup in the afternoon, but I really try not to overdo it. I don't want to get all jittery and make mistakes, you know? 

As for alcohol... oh, hardly ever. Maybe a glass of wine at a friend's wedding or a birthday dinner, but that's really it. And I definitely don't use any recreational drugs or anything like that! I promise. I try to be really responsible and take good care of my health. 

With medications, um, I just take a regular daily multivitamin. And maybe an ibuprofen every now and then if I get a headache from staring at my computer screen too long at work. But nothing prescribed, and nothing on a regular basis. 

I try to keep everything pretty clean and simple. I hope that's okay? Please let me know if you need me to be more specific about any of that!
Do these memory slips happen mainly when you're juggling multiple tasks or feeling rushed, or do you notice them even during quieter, less busy times when you're relaxed and not multitasking?

Um, well, I think it's mostly just when things get really crazy at the office. You know, like if the phones are ringing off the hook and my boss is asking me to pull three different files while I'm trying to draft an email... that's usually when a little detail might slip my mind. I feel like anyone would get a little mixed up when they're pulled in that many directions, right? 

When things are quiet and I just have one thing to focus on, I feel like I'm totally fine! I really try to stay organized and keep my desk neat so I don't miss anything when I'm relaxed. I don't think I'm doing too badly, considering how much I have on my plate right now. That makes sense, doesn't it? I mean, it's pretty normal to just get a little overwhelmed when it's super busy, right?
When these memory slips happen, how do you feel about them afterward—do they feel like a normal side effect of being busy, or do they genuinely worry you that something might be wrong?

Oh, um, I think they just feel like a normal side effect of being busy, really! I mean, I don't think there's anything actually *wrong* with me, you know? It's just... well, everyone forgets a thing or two when they have a million things going on at once. 

I definitely don't sit around worrying that my brain is broken or anything like that. I just tell myself I need to be a little more careful next time, maybe write things down on a sticky note if it's a crazy day. I really try my best to stay on top of it all. I'm just a normal person trying to keep up with a busy schedule, you know? That sounds pretty typical, right? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is!

If your boss and classmates hadn't mentioned anything about these memory slips, do you think you would have sought this appointment on your own, or was their feedback the main reason you decided to come in?

Oh, um, honestly? I don't think I would have come in at all if they hadn't said anything. I really didn't think it was that big of a deal! Like I said, I just figured I was having normal busy days. 

But when my boss gently pointed out a couple of dropped messages, and then a girl in my study group mentioned I'd asked the same question twice... well, I just wanted to make absolutely sure I wasn't dropping the ball, you know? I really pride myself on being a good employee and a good student. I want to make sure I'm doing everything right and not letting anyone down. 

So, yeah, it was really their feedback that brought me here. I just want to be proactive and make sure I'm functioning at my best for them. That's the right thing to do, isn't it? Just getting a little check-up to be safe?
On weekends or during breaks from your evening classes, when you have less on your plate, do you still notice these memory slips, or do they seem to disappear when things settle down?

Um, well, on the weekends... I feel like things are pretty much fine. When I'm just hanging out at home or running a few errands, I don't really have those same slip-ups. I mean, I guess occasionally I might walk into a room and forget what I went in there for, but everyone does that, right? 

When I don't have the phones ringing and my boss asking for things, I can just take my time. I feel like my memory is totally normal when I'm not under all that pressure. I try really hard to keep my personal life organized, so I don't think it's an issue when things settle down. That's usually how it works for most people when they get a break, isn't it? I really don't think it's anything to worry about outside of work and school.

Even though you feel these slips are mostly due to being busy, is there any part of you that's genuinely worried something might be changing with your memory or thinking, separate from just having a lot on your plate?

Oh, gosh, no. Um, I really hope I didn't make it sound like I think I have some awful brain disease or something! I definitely don't sit around worrying that my actual memory is failing or that I'm, you know, losing my mind. 

I mean, I'm only 36, so I should be perfectly fine, right? I really do just think it's the stress of trying to juggle the phones at the office and then keeping up with my evening classes. I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job and keeping everyone happy. I don't feel like there's any deep, underlying problem with my thinking at all. It really is just the busyness. I'm not crazy for thinking that, am I? I just want to make sure we're on the same page and I'm not overreacting by being here!
Would you say that trying to balance your job and evening classes feels genuinely stressful or overwhelming to you, even if you don't call it 'anxiety'?

Um, well, I guess... maybe a little bit? I mean, I wouldn't call it overwhelming, exactly. I really try to handle it all with a smile, you know? I want to be someone my boss can rely on, and I want to do well in my classes. 

It's just a lot to juggle sometimes, and I guess occasionally I feel a tiny bit stretched thin. But I'm definitely not falling apart or anything like that! I manage it okay most days. I think it's pretty normal to feel a little tired when you're working full-time and going to school, right? I just try to keep a positive attitude about it all. I hope that makes sense? I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining!
Have you had any extended time off from both work and classes recently—like a vacation—and if so, did the memory slips completely go away during that time?

Um, well, let me think... I haven't really had a long vacation recently. I mean, I took a couple of days off around the holidays, but I was still doing, you know, normal holiday stuff, so it wasn't exactly a break. 

I guess I haven't really had a chance to see what would happen if I just did absolutely nothing for a week or two. But I'm sure if I did, everything would be totally fine! I really think it's just the day-to-day juggling that trips me up sometimes. Does that make sense? I'm sorry I don't have a better answer for you, I just haven't really had the chance to test it out like that. I hope that's okay?
Has anyone ever given you a formal memory or cognitive test, and if not, would you be willing to have one now to see how your memory performs compared to what's expected for your age?

Oh, no, I've never had any kind of official test like that. Honestly, I've never really felt like I needed one! Um, but if you think it's something we should do, I'm definitely open to it. 

I mean, I'm sure it would just show that everything is normal, right? I'd be happy to take it if it helps you figure things out. I just... I really don't think there's anything seriously wrong with my brain. But I want to be cooperative and do whatever you think is best! Is that something we'd do today, or...? I just want to make sure I'm doing whatever you need me to do.
I'd like to do a brief memory and cognitive screening test with you right now, if that's okay—can we go ahead and do that together?

Um, yes, of course! We can definitely do that right now. I'm completely fine with it. 

Whatever you need to do is perfectly okay with me. I'm sure it'll be quick and easy, right? I just want to be helpful and make sure you have all the information you need. I'm ready whenever you are! I hope I do okay on it... I mean, I'm sure I will, but you know what I mean, right? Just let me know what you need me to do!
Let's start the screening: Can you tell me today's full date, and then repeat back these three words after me—apple, table, penny?

Um, yes, of course! Today is... let's see, it's Tuesday, October 24th, 2023. And the words are apple, table, penny. Did I get that right? I hope that's what you were looking for! I can say them again if you need me to.
A few minutes have passed since I gave you those three words—can you tell me now what they were?

Oh gosh... um. Apple? And... oh no, I'm so sorry, my mind just went completely blank on the other two. I feel so silly! I want to say... chair? No, that's not right. 

I'm really, really sorry. I was just trying so hard to focus on being helpful and answering your questions right, and they just slipped right out of my head. Is that okay? I promise my memory is normally fine, I think I just got a little nervous because it's a test and I want to do a good job for you. I hope I'm not messing up your evaluation! Am I doing alright otherwise?

doctor.question: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?
